extracted.intended_audience: educators, teachers, education theorists, and school policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for formulating and evaluating aims in education: what makes an aim valid, practical, and educative; contrasts natural-development and social-efficiency conceptions of aims and their practical implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim as foresight and intelligent action
rubrics_metrics.description: An aim denotes the result of any natural process brought to consciousness and made a factor in determining present observation and choice of ways of acting; it signifies foresight of the alternative consequences attendant upon acting in a given situation and the use of what is anticipated to direct observation and experiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the aim to direct observation and experiment; an aim is contrasted with an externally imposed end which is fixed and remote. Anti-pattern: treating 'aim' as mere label or final possession rather than as a guiding, experimental orientation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim must be an outgrowth of existing conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The aim set up must be an outgrowth of existing conditions; it must be based upon a consideration of what is already going on, upon the resources and difficulties of the situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical guidance: ground aims in current pupil experience, resources, and obstacles. Anti-patterns: adopting theories or ends 'lying outside our activities' or 'ready-made' aims imposed from without that ignore concrete conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim must be tentative, experimental, and flexible
rubrics_metrics.description: The aim as it first emerges is a mere tentative sketch; acting upon it brings to light overlooked conditions requiring revision. An aim must be flexible and capable of alteration to meet circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate aims by whether they are tested in action and revised; good aims grow as they are exercised. Scoring note: aims that cannot be modified in light of experience are defective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim must represent a freeing of activities (integration of ends and means)
rubrics_metrics.description: The aim must always represent a freeing of activities: the object (target) is a sign directing an activity which itself is the true end; ends should function as means and vice versa rather than as a static possession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer aims that make activity significant at every stage, treating intermediate achievements as ends-in-themselves. Anti-pattern: divorcing means from ends, which reduces activity to drudgery and makes aims rigid and oppressive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aims should assist observation, choice, and planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Any aim is of value so far as it assists observation, choice, and planning in carrying on activity from moment to moment and hour to hour; aims that 'get in the way of the individual's own common sense' do harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge aims by whether they improve a teacher's and pupil's capacity to observe, anticipate, and organize activities. Anti-pattern: aims that prevent ordinary judgment or exclude recognition of relevant details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational aims must be founded on the intrinsic activities and needs of the individual
rubrics_metrics.description: An educational aim must be founded upon the intrinsic activities and needs (including original instincts and acquired habits) of the given individual to be educated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims should recognize and start from a learner's native powers and present capacities; avoid setting adult-centered or uniform aims that neglect individual differences. Example: using adult achievements only as context, not as rigid end-points imposed on children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim must be translatable into cooperative methods and specific procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: An aim must be capable of translation into a method of cooperating with the activities of those undergoing instruction; it must suggest the kind of environment needed to liberate and organize their capacities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate aims by whether they 'lend themselves to the construction of specific procedures' that test, correct, and amplify the aim. Anti-pattern: aims so abstract they cannot guide classroom practice or testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against externally imposed, rigid, or abstract 'ultimate' ends
rubrics_metrics.description: Be on guard against ends that are alleged to be general and ultimate; abstract or remote ends detached from specific context lead to mechanical teaching and learning as mere preparation for a future disconnected from present activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for aims that connect directly to present activities; general aims are useful only insofar as they broaden outlook and inform concrete actions. Anti-pattern: treating 'education' as having a single final aim imposed top-down.

rubrics_metrics.name: General/comprehensive aims should broaden outlook and complement one another
rubrics_metrics.description: A truly general aim broadens the outlook; multiple comprehensive ends may exist without competition, each suggesting different questions and observations and thereby supplementing one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow plurality of stated aims to provide diverse perspectives and richer observation; do not force a single comprehensive aim to dominate practicable classroom decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural-development aim: emphasize health and bodily vigor
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural development as an aim fixes attention upon the bodily organs and the need of health and vigor; 'Make health an aim; normal development cannot be had without regard to the vigor of the body.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical implication: evaluate whether curricula and practices preserve and promote health. Anti-pattern: neglecting physical conditions that undermine other aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural-development aim: respect physical mobility and bodily activity
rubrics_metrics.description: The aim of natural development translates into regard for physical mobility: children are always in motion; bodily exercise (play, handling materials) plays a key role in mental development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess aims by whether they permit and organize physical exploration and activity rather than imposing sedentary or overly formal routines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural-development aim: attend to individual differences and timing of growth
rubrics_metrics.description: Following nature means regard for individual differences among children and attention to the origin, waxing and waning, of preferences and interests; capacities bud and bloom irregularly, so one must 'strike while the iron is hot.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims should enable recognition of spontaneous activities and capitalize on early manifestations of power. Anti-pattern: imposing uniform exercises that 'stunt the true gifts of nature.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Social-efficiency aim: industrial competency without perpetuating status quo
rubrics_metrics.description: Social efficiency translated into specific aims indicates the importance of industrial competency: ability to earn a living and use products of industry wisely; but training must not merely fit individuals to existing inequitable economic arrangements or lock them into too-specific occupations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate aims for whether they develop adaptable vocational competence and economic judgment while resisting narrow vocational tracking or reproduction of class privilege. Anti-pattern: training that anticipates fixed jobs tied to parental status or current industry structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social-efficiency aim: civic efficiency (good citizenship)
rubrics_metrics.description: Civic efficiency denotes qualifications ranging from agreeable social traits to the capacity to judge men and measures wisely and to take part in making as well as obeying laws; social efficiency ultimately means capacity to share in a give-and-take of experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess aims by whether they cultivate judgment, participation, and the ability to engage in public life; avoid too-narrow interpretations that exclude scientific or theoretical pursuits which ultimately support social progress.
